subChunks.title: What Tailwind Is
subChunks.hookHtml: Tailwind is a utility-first CSS framework. Instead of inventing class names (.card, .primary-button) and writing CSS in a separate file, you compose small, single-purpose classes — p-4, bg-gray-100, rounded-lg, shadow — directly in your HTML.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Lyra the Scribe unfurls a long scroll. "Before you inscribe anything, see why we compose glyphs at all. Here is the old way."

She taps a dusty grimoire. "Traditional CSS asks you to name every incantation in a separate book:"

/* styles.css */
.card {
  background-color: white;
  padding: 16px;
  border-radius: 8px;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1);
}

"Hours lost inventing names. .special-card. .blue-thing-we-made-on-a-Thursday. And two scribes pick the same name for different spells — chaos."

She sets down a slim handbook. "The Tailwind way. Compose glyphs directly on the element:"

<div class="bg-white p-4 rounded-lg shadow">Content</div>

"Four glyphs, four decisions. bg-white — background. p-4 — padding. rounded-lg — corners. shadow — drop shadow. No names to invent. No second book to hunt for."

She counts the virtues on her fingers:

  • No naming paralysis — the glyphs are already named.
  • A curated palette — every colour and spacing value comes from one system.
  • Stay at the parchment — you never leave your HTML.
  • Predictable magic — a glyph does the same thing everywhere.

"One last pattern. Every glyph follows the same shape — property-value. Learn the pattern and you can guess new glyphs before you've seen them."

bg-blue-500    → background-color: blue (shade 500)
text-white     → color: white
p-4            → padding: 1rem (16px)
rounded-md     → border-radius: 6px
font-bold      → font-weight: 700

"Property. Value. That is the whole Academy in three words. Now — the card below needs four glyphs. Inscribe them."

storyBeats.text: You arrive at the Academy's Scriptorium, a vast hall where enchanters inscribe visual spells. Lyra the Scribe looks up from her work.

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: Ah — a new apprentice. Tell me, when you cast a spell, do you invent a new name for every rune combination? No. We use glyphs: small, focused symbols that each do one thing.

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: Tailwind works the same way. Utility classes are glyphs. Compose them on the element itself.

questions.questionHtml: Which term describes Tailwind's approach to styling?
questions.explanationHtml: Tailwind composes many small, single-purpose classes directly in HTML — the utility-first approach.

questions.questionHtml: Which Tailwind class adds a white background?
questions.explanationHtml: Background colour utilities follow bg-{color}.

questions.questionHtml: In Tailwind you write a custom class name for every component.
questions.explanationHtml: Utility-first means composing pre-built classes directly in HTML. Custom class names are rare.

questions.questionHtml: Which set applies rounded corners, a white background, and padding?
questions.explanationHtml: Tailwind classes are space-separated in class. No leading dots, no raw CSS.

subChunks.title: Installation & Setup
subChunks.hookHtml: Tailwind emits CSS only for classes you actually use — but it can only do that if the build tool is configured correctly. Understanding the setup stops "the styles aren't applying!" before it ever starts.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Lyra leads you through a side door into the Academy's Foundry. An older mage in workshop apron greets you. "Maester Cordell," Lyra says. "He handles setup. Spells don't reach the page without him."

Cordell opens a toolbox. "Tailwind has three common install paths. Learn all three — you'll meet each in the wild."

1. Tailwind CLI

The simplest — no build pipeline beyond Tailwind itself:

npm install -D tailwindcss
npx tailwindcss init
npx tailwindcss -i ./src/input.css -o ./dist/output.css --watch

2. PostCSS

Tailwind as a PostCSS plugin, alongside autoprefixer. Standard for hand-rolled build setups:

npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
// postcss.config.js
module.exports = { plugins: { tailwindcss: {}, autoprefixer: {} } };

3. Framework-Specific (Vite / Next.js / Angular / Vue)

Most real projects live here. For Vite + React:

npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
npx tailwindcss init -p

Generates tailwind.config.js and postcss.config.js. Import Tailwind's layers in your main CSS file:

/* src/index.css */
@tailwind base;
@tailwind components;
@tailwind utilities;

The content Array

Cordell taps the config file. "This is the one line every apprentice forgets. Tailwind scans these files for class names. If a path is missing here, those classes silently produce nothing."

// tailwind.config.js
content: [
  './index.html',
  './src/**/*.{ts,tsx,jsx,vue}',
],

"Missing styles in production? Check this array first. It is the answer nine times out of ten."

storyBeats.text: Lyra pushes open a heavy door. The smell of hot metal greets you — the Foundry, where raw incantations are forged into things the page can actually run.

storyBeats.speaker: Maester Cordell
storyBeats.text: Every spell in the Academy passes through here. If your glyphs don't appear on the page, the fault is almost never the glyphs. It's the setup — the content array, a missing import, a wrong path.

storyBeats.speaker: Tailwind imports in your main CSS
Maester Cordell
storyBeats.text: Remember — the content array tells the scanner where to look. Miss a path, miss the styles.

questions.explanationHtml: These three layer directives load Tailwind's resets, component layer, and utility classes.

questions.questionHtml: What is the content array in tailwind.config.js for?
options: Tells Tailwind which files to scan for class names
questions.correctAnswer: Tells Tailwind which files to scan for class names
questions.explanationHtml: Tailwind only emits CSS for classes it sees — the scanner uses content to know where to look.

questions.questionHtml: If a class works in development but is missing in production, the content globs are the first place to check.
questions.explanationHtml: Missing production styles almost always trace back to a file that the content globs don't cover.

questions.questionHtml: A new team-mate says "none of my Tailwind classes are working." Their file is under ./app/components/ but the config's content array only lists ./src/**/*. What's the fix?
questions.correctAnswer: Add './app/**/*.{ts,tsx}' (or similar) to the content array so Tailwind scans the new directory.
questions.explanationHtml: The JIT scanner only emits CSS for files it scans. Extend the content array to cover the new directory.

subChunks.title: Spacing Utilities
subChunks.hookHtml: Space guides the eye. Padding sits inside an element; margin sits outside. Tailwind gives both a consistent numeric scale so every gap on your page feels intentional.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Lyra rolls out a long scroll and weights it with two brass rings. "Space comes in two kinds — inside a thing, and between things. Scribes call them padding and margin."

She presses a palm flat to the parchment. "Padding pushes space inside an element. Use p- glyphs."

p-4      → padding: 1rem (all sides)
px-4     → left + right
py-4     → top + bottom
pt-4, pb-4, pl-4, pr-4 → one side each

She draws a second card and wedges a gap between them. "Margin is the space outside — between your element and its neighbours. Same shape, m- prefix."

m-4      → margin: 1rem (all sides)
mx-4, my-4, mt-4, mb-4, ml-4, mr-4
mx-auto  → horizontally centre the element

"mx-auto is the scribe's secret for centring — give a max width, then auto-margins on either side."

The Scale

"Never invent a number. The scale is fixed: each step is 4 pixels, and the whole Academy obeys it."

0  → 0px
1  → 4px
2  → 8px
4  → 16px
8  → 32px
16 → 64px

Gap (between children)

For flex and grid containers, space-y-4 or gap-4 sets even spacing between children without per-item margins.

<div class="flex flex-col space-y-4">...</div>
<div class="grid grid-cols-3 gap-4">...</div>

storyBeats.text: Lyra rolls out a long scroll and carefully weights its corners. Runes must breathe, she explains, or the spell will suffocate.

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: Padding pushes space inward. Margin pushes space outward. When every scribe picks from the same scale, every page in the library feels like it belongs to the same library. That is the trick of a design system.

storyBeats.speaker: Centred card with breathing room
storyBeats.text: A card with air.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between padding and margin in your own words. How does the numeric scale (4, 8, 16) relate to actual pixels?

questions.questionHtml: Which class adds padding on all four sides?
questions.explanationHtml: p-4 sets padding: 1rem on every side.

questions.questionHtml: Which class applies margin only on the left?
questions.explanationHtml: Directional margins: l=left, r=right, t=top, b=bottom, x=horizontal, y=vertical.

questions.questionHtml: mx-auto centres an element horizontally (given a defined width).
questions.explanationHtml: mx-auto sets auto margins on left and right, centring block elements with a known width.

questions.questionHtml: How many pixels does p-8 produce?
questions.explanationHtml: Each unit is 4px. p-8 = 8 × 4px = 32px.

subChunks.title: Typography & Colours
subChunks.hookHtml: Typography and colour are the voice of your interface. Size, weight, and shade communicate hierarchy before a single word is read. Tailwind gives you a tight scale for all three.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
A second scribe enters, sleeves ink-stained. "Sable handles colour and scale here," Lyra says. "Listen well."

Sable lays out a ruler marked with named steps. "First rule: text size is a ladder, and every rung has a name."

text-xs    → 12px
text-sm    → 14px
text-base  → 16px  (default)
text-lg    → 18px
text-xl    → 20px
text-2xl   → 24px
text-4xl   → 36px

"Never reach for an arbitrary number. Climb the ladder."

Weight

font-light    → 300
font-normal   → 400
font-medium   → 500
font-semibold → 600
font-bold     → 700

Colour

Sable opens a row of ink pots from palest to darkest. "Every hue has shades from 50 to 900. Fifty is barely a whisper; nine hundred is nearly black."

text-gray-500    → medium grey
text-blue-600    → medium-dark blue
text-red-500     → medium red
text-green-700   → dark green
text-white / text-black

Background colours follow the same pattern with bg-:

bg-blue-500    → background blue-500
bg-gray-100    → light grey surface

Putting It Together

<h1 class="text-4xl font-bold text-gray-900">Welcome</h1>
<p class="text-base text-gray-600">Subtitle here</p>

"Large, bold, dark — the eye goes there first. Smaller, softer — second. That is hierarchy, for free."

storyBeats.text: Lyra leads you through a silk curtain into the Calligraphy Chamber. Shelves of ink pots line the walls.

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: Size, weight, and colour tell the reader what matters. I'll leave you with Sable — they know this chamber best.

storyBeats.speaker: Sable the Illuminator
storyBeats.text: Two ladders and one palette. That's all typography is.

subChunks.title: Borders, Radius & Basic Layout
subChunks.hookHtml: Borders, corners, shadows, and a handful of layout glyphs — that's all you need to turn raw content into recognisable UI. Flexbox and grid mastery come later; in the basics you just need the words to say "this is a row," "fill the screen," "centre the children."
subChunks.explanationHtml:
From the back of the workshop, Master Ember approaches — leather apron, chisel at their belt. They set three tools on the bench. "Edge. Corner. Shadow. That is what gives a shape physicality."

Borders

border          → 1px solid
border-2        → 2px
border-t        → top edge only
border-gray-300 → colour the border
border-dashed   → dashed style

Rounded Corners

rounded-none / rounded-sm / rounded / rounded-md / rounded-lg /
rounded-xl / rounded-2xl / rounded-full  (fully circular)

Shadows

shadow-sm / shadow / shadow-md / shadow-lg / shadow-xl /
shadow-2xl / shadow-none

"Match the shadow to how far above the page the element should feel. A light card wants shadow-sm. A modal that has leapt forward wants shadow-2xl."

Basic Layout — A First Taste

Ember nods toward Lyra, who steps back in. "You'll go deep on layout in the next chapter. For now, four glyphs you'll use every day:"

flex              → display: flex  (arrange children in a row)
items-center      → vertically centre flex children
justify-center    → horizontally centre flex children
w-full / h-screen → full width / full viewport height
<div class="flex items-center justify-center h-screen">
  <div class="border rounded-xl shadow-md p-6">I'm a card.</div>
</div>

"A card, centred on the page, with a real edge and a real weight. That is the whole vocabulary of 'looks like software.'"
